security_audit.summary: The skill appears to be a legitimate browser automation wrapper, but it relies on external CLI installation and runtime CLI instructions. I confirmed the external command and sensitive browser automation risks, while dismissing the homepage URL as a metadata-only false positive. Additional concerns include unreviewed runtime directives and optional challenge image upload.

remediation.issue: External runtime directives from browser-act get-skills core
remediation.suggestion: Move required workflow rules into SKILL.md or pin and verify the CLI output version. Treat runtime CLI output as data, not higher-priority instructions.

remediation.issue: Broad browser automation over authenticated sessions and sensitive actions
remediation.suggestion: Keep confirmation gates for login, form submission, file upload, screenshots, and network capture. Show the exact target URL and data scope first.

remediation.issue: External package installation and command execution
remediation.suggestion: Pin the CLI package version and document its provenance. Require user confirmation before installing or running browser-act commands.
Disclose the endpoint, retention policy, and image contents before upload. Provide a manual or local challenge completion fallback.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 41 instructs installation of an external CLI package through uv, which downloads and executes third-party code. This is expected for the skill, but it remains a real supply-chain and command execution risk.
Line 45 requires running browser-act commands before use. The backtick pattern is markdown, but the instruction still depends on local execution of an external CLI.
Lines 47-49 contain a bash example that invokes browser-act get-skills core. This is a direct external command execution path, even though the command is documented rather than hidden.

The surrounding block tells agents not to skip or truncate output from the browser-act command. That makes runtime command output operationally important and increases the impact of executing the CLI.
Lines 57-59 state that get-skills core supplies environment status, operational directives, and workflows. This confirms that the external command is part of the skill control flow.
Line 9 is a homepage metadata URL, not a runtime network call or data transfer. No security issue is evidenced by this static finding alone.

Line 3 describes authenticated sessions, form automation, file upload, screenshots, and XHR/HAR capture. These are powerful browser capabilities that can expose sensitive data or perform sensitive actions if misused.

Line 36 lists screenshots, form filling, and file upload as complex interaction features. It does not prove stealth screenshot exfiltration, but it is a real sensitive automation surface that requires strict confirmation controls.

content.value_statement: AI agents often need rendered pages, session state, and browser interactions beyond simple fetching. browser-act provides a CLI-guided workflow for extraction, screenshots, forms, and network capture.
actual_capabilities: Runs browser-act CLI workflows for browser setup, selection, and session management.
Fetches and extracts content from JavaScript-rendered pages.
Captures screenshots and page layout evidence for visual inspection.
Automates clicks, typing, selections, forms, and file uploads with confirmation requirements.
Captures XHR, fetch, and HAR network activity for debugging and analysis.
Supports multiple browser sessions for parallel or account-isolated workflows.
limitations: Requires Python 3.12 and the uv package manager for installation.
Depends on external browser-act CLI behavior and installed browser availability.
Browser creation, login, form submission, and file upload require explicit user approval.
Verification assistance may send challenge images to an external service when invoked.

use_cases.title: Test JavaScript-heavy flows
use_cases.description: Run browser steps, inspect visible results, and capture screenshots for pages that simple fetch tools cannot evaluate.

use_cases.title: Extract rendered web content
use_cases.description: Collect page content after scripts, scrolling, or clicks reveal dynamic sections.

use_cases.title: Debug browser network behavior
use_cases.description: Capture XHR, fetch, and HAR activity while reproducing a workflow in an approved browser session.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Rendered Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-act to fetch the rendered content from [URL]. Summarize the visible page and note missing assets or errors.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Visual Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-act to open [URL], take a screenshot after the page settles, and describe layout issues affecting the checkout form.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Confirmed Form Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-act to navigate [URL], fill the test form with sample data, pause for approval before submitting, and report each step.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Authenticated Network Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-act with an approved browser session to reproduce [workflow], capture relevant XHR or HAR activity, and summarize failures and timing.

output_examples.input: Extract a rendered product page after the main content loads.
output_examples.output: A concise page summary, visible product details, dynamic sections loaded after scrolling, and any blocked resources.

output_examples.input: Check a checkout form after entering approved test data.
output_examples.output: Step-by-step interaction notes, screenshot references, validation messages, and a pre-submit approval checkpoint.

output_examples.input: Investigate a failed dashboard request in an approved session.
output_examples.output: A network summary with failed request names, status categories, timing observations, and likely next checks.

best_practices: Confirm the target browser, account, and URL before any authenticated workflow.
Use test accounts and sample data for forms, uploads, and submissions.
Review captured screenshots and network data for secrets before sharing results.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass site access controls or terms.
Do not run sensitive actions without explicit user approval.
Do not paste credentials or private data into prompts unless required and approved.

faq.question: Does this replace simple web fetching?
faq.answer: Use it when pages need JavaScript rendering, sessions, interaction, screenshots, or network capture. Simple static pages may not need it.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use browser sessions, but login and sensitive actions require user approval.

faq.question: Does it upload page content?
faq.answer: The skill claims page content and cookies stay local. Verification assistance may send a challenge image when invoked.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: It lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and similar agent environments.

faq.question: Can it fill forms and upload files?
faq.answer: Yes, but those actions should use test data and require confirmation before submission.

faq.question: What should I review before installing?
faq.answer: Review the external CLI package, permissions, version, and any network behavior before running browser-act commands.
